title: Armstrong's dominance over the trumpet section and guests
summary: Armstrong made the other trumpets sound small, as did a radio appearance where a guest trumpeter faltered beside him.

story.theme_name: Working with and around Louis Armstrong
story.community_name: Playing with and around Louis Armstrong

blocks.x: Louis would just come on and do an hour or so. He would do his spot and then the band would play over.

But if they play together, which they have, well they play together, we had arrangements where you were Red. But I tell you one thing, if it was something in unison, and with the three trumpets and Louis together, Louis would make the rest of them sound like little boys. Really? Oh yes. Oh yes. We have arrangements to prove it. Alexander's Ragtime Band. Heart full of rhythm. Get the big band. And you hear Red and all of them, they sound like little boys. Yes.
Well it just shows how fantastic Armstrong was at that time. Because you hear records like Feeling Drowsy and Swing Out, which Red Allen featured on those. Very nice. Very tremendous.
And to think that Louis could go here.

Oh man, Louis blew them all into bad health. I remember one time in New York on Rudy Blesher's program, This Is Jazz, and Louis was a guest star for that Saturday. And Bill Davidson was on that program. And Louis played two, three numbers with the group, with our regular group. And when Pops took over, Bill Davidson sounded like a little boy amateur. And he couldn't play it no more the rest of the evening. He was so nervous. Because he didn't have the sound. The master was there, man. That's something else. You don't have no, you only have one Louis. And I'd say you had one Bechet. You see what I mean? You had one Dodds. These are outstanding people, man. Nobody sounds, you know, when they're on a session with you, I'm sorry. You don't have to the problem.
